spec: docs/plans/2026-09-11-nodus-ledger-snapshot-design.md section 8.9 FINAL — normative byte spec (C1-C7, S1-S8)
label: SELF-CONSISTENT (independent re-implementation of the same document; not an external reference)

conventions.integers: big-endian in preimages; decimal strings in JSON
conventions.merkle: C6: n==1 -> leaf; pairs SHA3-512(node_tag|L|R); odd last node carried up unchanged
conventions.inputs: byte strings = SHA3-512('hf7_root_coverage_kat/' + label); random integers = first 8 bytes of such a digest, big-endian, shifted right to the type width; fixed = constant byte patterns / 0 / type maximum
conventions.errors: each error vector has one defect; 'error' is the oracle's reason string (reason class is normative, exact wording is not)

ambiguities: R1 S6 enc89 fields (domain_id u32, domain_height u64, last_updated_global_height u64, ruleset_version u32, status u8) have no stated range in 8.9; the range is the full width of the type (C3 errors only outside it). status is not restricted to any value set.

R2 Opaque 64-byte inputs (S4 L1..L9 and its three new legs, S5 Root(k), S6 domain_state_root / last_upd_hash, S8 domains_root / replay_root) are checked for length only (C4); their content is not interpreted.

R3 C4 "fixed length as written": a byte string of the wrong length (or a non-bytes value) is treated as an ERROR, although the KAT obligations paragraph does not list that case. Such vectors are emitted (S1, S5, S7, S8).

R4 C3: a non-integer (including bool) where an integer is written is an ERROR. Integers are checked against the STATED range of the item (e.g. S1 amount 0..2^63-1, S7 expiry 1..2^64-1), not only the type width.

R5 S7 "both tx_id and intent_id unique across the set": uniqueness is per column. A tx_id equal to some other row's intent_id is NOT an error. tx_id uniqueness follows from the strict ascending order of C5 and is reported as "duplicate key"; intent_id uniqueness is a separate check reported as "duplicate intent_id".

R6 "S4, S6, S8 with fixed and with random inputs": "fixed" = constant byte patterns (all 0x00, all 0xFF, per-input constant byte) and fixed integers (0, type maximum, or the per-input constant byte value); "random" = deterministic pseudo-random inputs, every byte string = SHA3-512("hf7_root_coverage_kat/" + label) and every integer = the leading bytes of such a digest, big-endian, shifted to the type width. No `random` module, no unseeded source.
R7 C6 Merkle inputs are the 64-byte leaf HASHES (S1/S3/S5/S7 leaves, S6 head hashes); n == 1 root = that hash itself (no node tag applied).
R8 The root functions REFUSE non-canonical input (C5) instead of sorting it; the KAT generator sorts its own valid inputs before calling them.

R9 When an input has more than one defect, the error reported is the first one detected, in this check order: (S6 only) empty list; per row in row order, each field in written order (type, length, range); (S6 only) first head not domain 0; key order (equal neighbour -> "duplicate key", descending neighbour -> "unsorted keys"); (S7 only) duplicate intent_id. The ERROR vectors each carry exactly one defect, so this order does not change any expected result.
R10 S2 "absent" is represented as JSON null / Python None.
R11 S6 "first being domain 0": the first head's domain_id must equal 0; an equal domain_id neighbour is the C5 "duplicate key" ERROR.

R12 JSON: byte strings are lowercase hex; integers are decimal strings (exact for u64 and for out-of-range values such as 2^64). Every leaf / vstat / head / composition also carries its full preimage hex, which pins the big-endian encoding independently of the decimal fields.

errors.name: only_8_v5_legs
errors.error: SYSTEM v6 needs exactly 9 v5 legs
